typed: I grab the leather satchel from beside the dead man and open it to see what the message is.
note: Good opening scene, vivid. Nothing confusing.

typed: I shove the letter into my habit and square up to the officer. "Make me hand it over, old man." I go for a fight if he draws steel.
note: Fine. The letter's contents are intriguing. Skabka's offer to name the recipient is a nice hook.

typed: I keep the letter and shove Milby hard in the chest, then throw a punch at him.
note: Nice tension. Milby's offer was clear, though no menu of options was shown, so I'm pushing for the fight.
Odds screen is clear. One small oddity: "Martial +1" though my character is an acolyte with Might 0. Otherwise fine.

Pressing "go big" just gave me the same offer again with identical odds and stakes, so I can't tell what going big changed. The narration also treated my shove-then-punch as if it hadn't happened. Committing now.
Near-miss screen is clear enough. Odd that the earlier screen said "Close call (15%)" and I got it, fine. No complaints.

typed: /fix The result line says "Changed: your opponent worn" which is cut off or garbled. It should say what changed, like Milby being hurt or worn down.
note: The result line "Changed: your opponent worn" reads as a truncated phrase. The fight itself was vivid, and the near-miss choice menu was clear.

typed: I scramble up and swing again at Milby's jaw before he can draw.
note: The fix reply was fine, though "worn" is a bit vague as a state. Otherwise the fight is clear and the near-miss menu worked well.
Odds screen is clear, though the same offer text repeats nearly verbatim. Note the "Prone" condition didn't appear in the offer's odds (still 60%) even though I'm in the mud, which seems odd.
Odds screen is clear; go-big note explained the raised stakes well. Fine.

typed: I jab him again in the ribs and snarl, "Tell me who the letter was meant for, Milby, and maybe I'll let you keep your teeth."
note: The blow landed fine, but the result line again says "your opponent worn" with no name. The /fix last time didn't change the wording. Otherwise this was clear and vivid.

typed: I turn to face the gate men walking toward us and draw myself up, hand on the satchel. "Come and take it, then."
note: Fine. Milby's earlier "tell me who it was for" went nowhere, but the new threat from the gate is a good hook.

typed: I knock the spear tip aside with my forearm and lunge at the lead guard, swinging for his face.
note: Good tension. Note the last two turns gave no odds screen or roll; the jab and the defiant speech were resolved straight in prose. Fine, but I expected an offer.
The odds screen is clear. Odd that the "Badly" chance jumps to 20% here, but I like the risk. Also the offer says "Hurt the lead guard's face" while the guard hasn't actually been engaged yet, fine.
